title: Redwood All-Hands: March Leadership Update
customer_attendees: Engineering, Product, Sales, CS, Ops, Security teams
summary: Monthly all-hands covering Q1 results, product roadmap highlights (Dedicated, Private, Optimize), hiring and org updates, security/compliance progress, and an extended Q&A. Deck shared after the meeting.
topics: Security & compliance updates (SOC 2, audit logs, KMS)
next_steps: Share the slide deck and recording (Lina to share link)
Follow-up survey to collect questions and product feedback (Tom)
Schedule smaller customer-focused deep dives on Dedicated/Private (sales+product)
Security team to publish latest SOC 2 readiness checklist
action_items: Lina Zhou: upload slides & link to #all-hands by 2026-03-11
Tom Becker: send out the post-all-hands survey by 2026-03-12
Miguel Alvarez & Infra leads: run internal perf benchmark plan and share results by 2026-03-24
Priya Nair: share Q1 revenue and burn details with leadership by 2026-03-13
transcript:
[00:00] Sarah (CEO): Good morning everyone, thanks for joining the March all-hands. Uh we have a packed agenda, we'll run through the numbers, product updates, and then do Q and A. Quick note the deck's in drive, I'll drop the link in chat after.
[00:35] Miguel (CTO): Hi all, I'll kick off with infra and reliability. Q1 our p99 on hosted API improved, still some tail with larger sequences and cold KV cache misses, we implemented a new prefix cache warming strategy. Uh the numbers look promising but there are still workloads hitting the tail at 200 to 400ms above target.
[01:10] Priya (CFO): From finance, Q1 SaaS ARR growth came in slightly above plan, MRR up 8%. We're managing spend on spot/reserved GPU capacity, dedicated commit uptake helped unit economics. We'll share details in the finance channel.
[01:45] Lina (Product): Roadmap highlights: Dedicated GA improvements — autoscale policies, burst capacity, and better telemetry in console. Private: VPC onboarding flow simplified, and we're adding KMS integrations and audit log improvements. Optimize: batching/caching suggestion engine 1.0, and quantization recommendations by workload.
[02:20] Sarah: A few wins — three mid-market deals closed this quarter including one large FINTECH customer that required dedicated and stricter data residency controls. Shoutout to Sales and Solutions for moving that.
[02:55] Audience (murmur): applause / claps
[03:10] Tom (People): Hiring update: we remain on track for the engineering hiring plan, though some roles like infra SRE and inference engine specialists are higher priority. We'll open a follow-up AMAs for interview calibration. Also updating parental leave policy, details in #people.
[03:45] Miguel: Quick tech deep dive summary: kernel selection improvements reduced infer latency by ~6% in our internal tests. There's ongoing work to make quantized execution paths more robust across model families — some artifacts still appear for 4-bit int quant. Note, some of the model names in the runbook are spelled inconsistently, we'll clean that up.
[04:20] Sarah: On go-to-market, we want to double down on developer-first content — tutorials, quickstarts and benchmark pieces. We saw traffic lift after the last benchmark blog. Remember our differentiation is serving economics, not just model access.
[04:55] Audience question (from Slack): Are we getting pushback on Hosted pricing vs Dedicated?
[05:10] Priya: Yes, some customers evaluate hosted first, then transition to Dedicated for predictable unit costs. We now have clearer comms on when to recommend dedicated vs hosted; product adds a banner for cost tipping points.
[05:45] Lina: Also adding more transparent cost controls in Console — token-level breakdown, per-route budgets.
[06:10] Audience (someone): Could you say more about Private / on-prem options and the network setup?
[06:25] Miguel: Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem bundle. There's a small installer we hand to infra teams; it requires some manual networking steps now but we're working on automating that. We also improved KMS/HSM support but note customers vary on key rotation policies, so we provide flexible integration paths.
[06:55] Sarah: Security & compliance — we're progressing on SOC 2 readiness, documentation is almost complete, and the security team is coordinating with external auditors. We'll publish an interim readiness checklist next week.
[07:30] Audience crosstalk: quick clarifications about audit scope, retention windows
[07:50] Miguel: On perf and benchmarks — a reminder that benchmarks are workloads dependent; we need to be careful about public claims. The team will publish per-model and per-hardware profiles, plus knobs: batching sizes, KV cache TTLs, and quant profiles.
[08:25] Audience (someone): Any changes to SLAs for hosted API or Dedicated?
[08:40] Lina: No immediate SLA changes for hosted; for Dedicated we are formalizing an SLA with latency/uptime targets as part of the committed contracts.
[09:00] Sarah: People questions — burnout risk and remote work policy. We heard the feedback, will roll out a new focus time policy and encourage time off. Leadership will host monthly AMAs.
[09:30] Tom: Also equity refresh schedule coming for managers, HR will share calendar.
[09:50] Miguel: Tech note — we're experimenting with smarter routing policies: route by latency, cost, and region; fallback to quantized variants when high load. Early tests show better availability during load spikes.
[10:20] Audience: cheers
[10:35] Sarah: Now to customer stories — Sales highlight, Jenna closed a big POC with a healthcare customer; they required private deployment and strict data retention. Great cross-functional effort.
[11:05] Jenna (Sales): It took three weeks to validate throughput for their workflows, we used dedicated nodes and ran a small benchmark sheet. Their security team asked for sample audit logs which we provided.
[11:40] Audience: applause
[12:00] Q&A start — open mics.
[12:15] Audience (Eng): Is there a plan to support more model variants in the catalog?
[12:30] Lina: Yes, model onboarding is prioritized; we're standardizing performance profiles and adding metadata so customers can select based on latency/cost/quality.
[12:55] Audience (Customer Success): Any new observability features?
[13:10] Miguel: Token-level cost, per-route tracing, and better error aggregation are in console roadmap; linking traces across retries is on the list.
[13:40] Audience (someone): A question about KV cache — how do we handle cold starts?
[13:55] Miguel: Warm-up strategies, prefix caching, and async prefetch jobs help. There's still work to do for very long context windows.
[14:20] Audience member interrupts: "we saw an outage last week, what happened?"
[14:30] Sarah: Yes, quick post-mortem — root cause was a misconfigured autoscaler in a Dedicated pool, cascading overload on the fallback path. The incident report is in #incident-ops. We've since tightened autoscaler defaults.
[15:05] Priya: On metrics, customer churn is flat; net new logo velocity is improving but conversion time from POC to commit remains a focus area. We want to shorten that by providing clearer success criteria.
[15:40] Audience (someone): Any new channel partnerships?
[15:55] Sarah: We're exploring a cloud marketplace listing for one provider in APAC and building an SI partner program.
[16:20] Tom: Culture note — town halls and team offsite plans are being organized; expect invites soon.
[16:45] Audience (someone): A few people asked about tooling for running internal benchmarks — is there a standard kit?
[17:00] Miguel: Yes, the infra team will publish a benchmarking harness and templates; it'll live in our internal repo with docs.
[17:30] Q&A continues with short questions on hiring, docs, and product feature prioritization.
[20:00] Sarah: Ok, quick recap: we'll share deck & recording, security to publish SOC 2 checklist, infra to run perf benchmarks, and people to send survey. Thanks all.
[20:20] Audience: applause and sign off
[58:30] [recording stops]
